problem: Let $A$  be the set of all multiples of $3$ greater than $0$ and let $B$  be the set of all multiples of $4$ greater than $0.$ What is $B-A?$

feedback.problem: Let $S$  be the set of all multiples of $2$ greater than $0$ and let $T$  be the set of all multiples of $4$ greater than $0.$ What is $T∖S?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The multiples of $2$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
S={2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,…}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
T={4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32,36,…}.
$$

Now, $T∖S$ is the *difference* of $T$ and $S,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $T$ but *not* in $S.$

The elements of $T$ that are also in $S$ are $4,8,12,16,$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $4$). So, we must remove these elements from $T.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T∖S & ={4,8,12,16,…}-{2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,…} \\  & =∅.\end{aligned}
$$
